propertyCopy: Corner radius, size and row dividers are properties of the same component, not separate lists - change them below to check this list's types and states in the Live Preview.
guide: Component Guide Human View Machine View Overview List displays a collection of similar items as stacked rows, like a notification feed, a team member roster, or a file browser - a straightforward vertical arrangement, simpler than Table's fixed columns and lighter than wrapping every item in its own Card. When to Use A notification feed or activity log - chronological or otherwise ordered similar entries. A team member roster or file browser - a stack of comparable items, each following the same row layout. A search results list - results that don't need Table's rigid column structure. When Not to Use Data organized around several comparable columns per row - use Table, which is built for column-aligned structured data. A small number of visually distinct, self-contained content blocks - use Card, or a grid of Cards, when items need their own visual containment. A single set of label/value pairs describing one thing - use Description instead of a list of one. Best Practices Keep row layout consistent across every item, even when some items have more content than others (use consistent placeholders/spacing). Show dividers or subtle spacing between rows so individual items stay scannable in a long list. Pair with Pagination or infinite scroll once the list grows beyond a comfortably scrollable length. Do and Don't Do MKMaya KhanCommented on Invoice #4021 One event per row, each with an actor and a specific object, so scanning the list tells a clear story. Don't UpdateSomething changed in the system related to a record that was recently modified by a user in the workspace. A vague title with a paragraph explaining nothing concrete forces the user to read every row in full to find out what actually happened. Accessibility Implemented with real list semantics (ul/li or role="list"/"listitem"), so screen readers announce item count and position. Interactive rows (clickable to open a detail view) are real links or buttons, not divs with only a click handler. Any per-row action (like a remove or edit icon) has an accessible name identifying which item it applies to.
